split_reasoning: Software acquisition and use standards and information-protection standards normally produce different policy documents.

parts.text: Develop standards and guidelines for acquiring and using software.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces written standards for others to follow.
parts.unit_reasoning: A standards document is reviewed and issued as a whole.
parts.work_item: one software acquisition and use standards document
parts.start: need for a new or revised standard identified
parts.end: standards document submitted for approval or issued
parts.overlap_reasoning: Technology recommendations can inform standards but address particular performance needs.

parts.text: Develop standards and guidelines for protecting vulnerable information.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces written security guidance.
parts.unit_reasoning: A security standards document is reviewed and issued as a whole.
parts.work_item: one information-protection standards document
parts.start: need for new or revised protection guidance identified
parts.end: guidance submitted for approval or issued
parts.overlap_reasoning: Security planning and access specifications apply or inform the standards but produce different outputs.

notes: Shares are estimates; some organizations combine these standards in one policy.

split_reasoning: Making database changes and directing other staff to make them are different activities.

parts.text: Modify an existing database or database management system.
parts.type_reasoning: Each assigned change produces a modified database or system.
parts.unit_reasoning: A requested change is implemented and handed over as a whole.
parts.work_item: one database or DBMS change implemented
parts.start: change requirement or request received
parts.end: change implemented and handed over
parts.overlap_reasoning: Error corrections, security changes, schema descriptions, and upgrades can involve database modifications but also have distinct scopes.

parts.text: Direct programmers or analysts making changes to an existing database or DBMS.
parts.type_reasoning: The part is supervision and direction of colleagues rather than a separate finished change made by the administrator.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Directing others to code database descriptions can be one kind of direction on a change.

notes: Shares vary with how much implementation is delegated.

split_reasoning: Testing produces findings, while correcting errors and modifying the program or database produces a separate change.

parts.text: Test a program or database and record the results.
parts.type_reasoning: A test produces results that others use to assess the program or database.
parts.unit_reasoning: A test run or test cycle has a coherent set of results.
parts.work_item: one program or database test cycle and its results
parts.start: program or database selected for testing
parts.end: test results and defects recorded or communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Testing changes is a subset of testing programs and databases.

parts.text: Correct errors and make necessary modifications to a program or database.
parts.type_reasoning: Each correction results in a changed program or database.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assigned correction or related set of modifications is handed over as a change.
parts.work_item: one error correction or related modification
parts.start: error or required modification identified
parts.end: correction implemented and handed over
parts.overlap_reasoning: Database modifications and DBMS upgrades may include corrections but also cover changes not prompted by errors.

notes: Testing and correction may be iterated; shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: Planning security measures and implementing them produce different outputs; coordination is included with planning.

parts.text: Plan and coordinate measures to safeguard computer-file information.
parts.type_reasoning: The planning work produces a set of measures for approval and implementation.
parts.unit_reasoning: A security plan for a defined system or change is reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one security measures plan
parts.start: system protection need or risk identified
parts.end: measures documented and coordinated for implementation
parts.overlap_reasoning: Protection standards and access specifications can form inputs to or components of a security plan.

parts.text: Implement measures to protect information in computer files.
parts.type_reasoning: Implementation produces a configured protection measure that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined security change is implemented and handed over as a whole.
parts.work_item: one security measure implemented
parts.start: protection measure approved or assigned
parts.end: measure configured and implementation communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Implementing a security measure can involve a database modification or application of access specifications.

notes: The balance between planning and implementation depends on the security measure.

split_reasoning: Planning, scheduling, and approving an installation produce a plan or approval, while supervising the work is a separate live activity.

parts.text: Plan, schedule, and approve installation and testing of a new product or system improvement.
parts.type_reasoning: This produces an installation and testing plan and approval for a defined change.
parts.unit_reasoning: The plan and approval are handled for a particular installation or improvement.
parts.work_item: one installation and testing plan with approval
parts.start: proposed product installation or improvement received
parts.end: plan and schedule approved and communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Upgrade planning and actual testing can be part of the installation process but have their own outputs.

parts.text: Supervise staff installing and testing a new product or system improvement.
parts.type_reasoning: Supervising staff is principally a live interpersonal activity.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Supervision may accompany upgrades or testing, without being the same work as performing them.

notes: Shares depend on the scale of the installation and level of delegation.

split_reasoning: Training and answering questions are different activities, and questions are handled both live and from written requests.

parts.text: Train users in database use.
parts.type_reasoning: The value of training is in the live teaching interaction.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Technical support may include teaching a user during a support interaction.

parts.text: Answer a user's database question during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The user waits while the administrator answers or looks up the answer.
parts.unit_reasoning: One question is addressed and communicated within the contact.
parts.work_item: one user question answered during a live contact
parts.start: user asks the question
parts.end: answer communicated to the user
parts.overlap_reasoning: Answering a user question can be part of technical support, which also covers troubleshooting and junior-staff assistance.

parts.text: Answer a user's database question received in writing.
parts.type_reasoning: The written answer is delivered without the user waiting in a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each written question receives an answer the user can rely on.
parts.work_item: one written user question answered
parts.start: written question received
parts.end: answer sent to the user
parts.overlap_reasoning: Written answers may be technical support, which also covers other support activities and recipients.

notes: Shares depend on training responsibilities and the channels users use.

split_reasoning: Identifying users and their access levels is one access-specification activity.

parts.text: Specify users and access levels for database segments.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces an access specification used to assign or review permissions.
parts.unit_reasoning: A set of access requirements for a database or defined change is reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one database access specification
parts.start: access requirements or a change request received
parts.end: users and access levels specified and communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Access specifications support security standards and measures but do not encompass all security planning or implementation.

split_reasoning: Pen, templates, and software are alternative tools for producing the same data model.

parts.text: Develop a data model describing data elements and their uses.
parts.type_reasoning: The model is a distinct artifact used by designers and developers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A model for a defined database or change is reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one data model
parts.start: data requirements and modeling scope received
parts.end: model completed and submitted for review
parts.overlap_reasoning: Database descriptions and data dictionary definitions may use or reflect a data model but are distinct artifacts.

split_reasoning: The target is one activity: consulting DBMS procedures to understand how to make a change.

parts.text: Review DBMS manual procedures needed for a database change.
parts.type_reasoning: The review informs subsequent work but does not itself specify a separate output that another person checks or relies on.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Manual review can support a modification or upgrade, but those statements cover the implemented change.

notes: If a workplace requires a documented procedure assessment, that assessment could be coded as a discrete item.

split_reasoning: Configuring performance monitoring and creating production databases produce different operational outputs.

parts.text: Select and enter code to monitor database performance.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a configured monitoring script or mechanism.
parts.unit_reasoning: A monitoring configuration for a defined database or need is deployed as a unit.
parts.work_item: one database performance monitoring configuration
parts.start: monitoring requirement identified
parts.end: monitoring code entered and operational
parts.overlap_reasoning: A monitoring configuration may involve modifying a DBMS, but database modification also covers other changes.

parts.text: Select and enter code to create a production database.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a production database for operational use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A database is created and handed over as a whole.
parts.work_item: one production database created
parts.start: approved database specification received
parts.end: production database created and handed over
parts.checked_by: database operations team and application owner
parts.overlap_reasoning: Creating a database may use coded database descriptions and form part of a planned installation.

notes: Shares vary with the frequency of production database creation.

split_reasoning: Identifying and evaluating trends are steps in providing management with trend information and advice.

parts.text: Evaluate database-system industry trends and advise upper management.
parts.type_reasoning: The evaluation produces advice or an assessment that management can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment of a defined trend or set of trends is communicated as a whole.
parts.work_item: one database-system trend assessment or briefing
parts.start: trend or management information need identified
parts.end: assessment and advice communicated to management
parts.overlap_reasoning: A trend assessment can inform a technology recommendation, but recommendations address a specific performance need.

notes: Advice may be written or presented in a briefing.

split_reasoning: Coding database descriptions and directing others to code them are different activities.

parts.text: Code logical and physical database descriptions and specify their identifiers to the DBMS.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces database definitions that the DBMS and development team use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A set of definitions for a database or defined schema change is submitted or applied as a whole.
parts.work_item: one coded set of database definitions
parts.start: database design or definition change received
parts.end: descriptions and identifiers coded and submitted or applied
parts.overlap_reasoning: Definitions can implement a data model, revise a database, or support creation of a production database, but those tasks have broader or different outputs.

parts.text: Direct others coding logical and physical database descriptions.
parts.type_reasoning: The activity is live direction of colleagues doing the coding.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Directing database modifications can include directing the coding of database descriptions.

split_reasoning: Reviewing a workflow chart to understand system tasks is one activity.

parts.text: Review a programmer analyst's workflow chart to understand the computer tasks.
parts.type_reasoning: The stated purpose is understanding the chart, not producing a separate checked output.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Understanding a workflow can inform database design or changes, but those statements cover separate outputs.

notes: A formal annotated chart or review finding would be a discrete item if required in a particular workplace.

split_reasoning: Revising company data definitions in the data dictionary is one activity.

parts.text: Revise company data definitions in the data dictionary.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces updated definitions that other staff rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A requested set of related dictionary changes is reviewed and published together.
parts.work_item: one set of related data dictionary revisions
parts.start: need to change data definitions identified
parts.end: revised definitions entered and communicated or published
parts.overlap_reasoning: Dictionary definitions relate to data models and coded database descriptions but are distinct maintained artifacts.

split_reasoning: Identifying and evaluating technologies are steps toward one recommendation for a database performance need.

parts.text: Evaluate and recommend hardware or software for a database performance need.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a recommendation that decision-makers can review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A recommendation addresses a defined performance requirement and is submitted as a whole.
parts.work_item: one database technology recommendation
parts.start: performance requirement or problem identified
parts.end: evaluated recommendation submitted
parts.overlap_reasoning: Trends and software standards can inform a recommendation, while an upgrade is a separate implementation.

split_reasoning: Planning and installing a DBMS upgrade are connected steps in delivering an upgrade; the target does not specify a separate planning handoff.

parts.text: Plan and install a DBMS software upgrade to improve database performance.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces an upgraded DBMS environment for operational use.
parts.unit_reasoning: An upgrade to a defined environment is planned, installed, and handed over as a unit.
parts.work_item: one DBMS upgrade installed
parts.start: upgrade need or approved upgrade identified
parts.end: upgrade installed and handed over to operations
parts.checked_by: database operations team and system owner
parts.overlap_reasoning: An upgrade is a system modification and may involve installation planning, technology evaluation, manual review, correction, and testing.

notes: In some organizations the upgrade plan is separately approved before installation.

split_reasoning: Technical support is provided both during live contacts and asynchronously from written requests.

parts.text: Provide technical support to a junior staff member or client during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The recipient waits while the administrator investigates or provides assistance.
parts.unit_reasoning: The live assistance for a specific issue is communicated within the contact.
parts.work_item: one technical support issue addressed during a live contact
parts.start: junior staff member or client requests help
parts.end: assistance or next step communicated during the contact
parts.overlap_reasoning: User questions and training can form part of technical support, which also includes troubleshooting and junior-staff assistance.

parts.text: Provide technical support to a junior staff member or client from a written request.
parts.type_reasoning: The administrator investigates and responds without the requester waiting in a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: An individual support request is investigated and answered or handed off as a unit.
parts.work_item: one asynchronous technical support request addressed
parts.start: written support request received
parts.end: resolution or next step sent to the requester
parts.checked_by: the staff member or client and support lead
parts.overlap_reasoning: Answering a written user question can be part of support, which also includes other technical issues and recipients.

notes: Channel shares vary by workplace and support arrangements.

split_reasoning: Testing changes to applications or systems is one activity; the two are alternative test subjects.

parts.text: Test a change to a database application or system.
parts.type_reasoning: Testing produces results and identified defects for the change team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A test cycle for a particular change is reported as a whole.
parts.work_item: one database change test cycle and its results
parts.start: change made available for testing
parts.end: test results and defects recorded or communicated
parts.checked_by: change owner, developers, and database lead
parts.overlap_reasoning: General program and database testing includes change testing, while upgrade and installation tasks may include testing their particular changes.
